subject: Order form: segmented entity billing, commit triggers & tax matrix
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Andrew Cho <andrew.cho@emergent.ai>, Emergent Procurement <procurement@emergent.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Order form: segmented entity billing, commit triggers & tax matrix

Andrew / Procurement team —

Thanks for the quick intro call earlier. Per our discussion, attaching a fresh draft of the order form (redwood_orderform_draft_v2.pdf) and a simple spreadsheet showing how we can route invoices to different Emergent entities based on PO/BU (orderform_entity_routing_table.xlsx). A couple of points for confirmation so our legal & finance teams can prepare redlines: 

- Invoice entity: you mentioned Emergent Solutions, Inc. and a separate financing entity (Emergent Financing LLC). Which entity will issue the PO(s)? We can invoice either or split across entities but need explicit PO mapping.
- Minimum commit triggers: we proposed a 3-tranche approach (initial commit, ramp at month 4, annual true-up). Confirm whether you want commits to be billed upfront or invoiced over the ramp period.
- Net terms: standard is Net 30; you asked about Net 60 on the call — please confirm preferred terms and any internal approval lead times.
- Taxes/withholding: please attach any tax certificates for non-US withholding or VAT registration. For cross-border withholdings (e.g., LATAM), we typically require customer evidence to apply net-of-withholding treatment.

Next steps: if you can (1) confirm invoice entity mapping and PO cadence, (2) share tax certs, and (3) flag net terms preference, I’ll loop in our commercial counsel for targeted redlines.

Attachments: redwood_orderform_draft_v2.pdf, orderform_entity_routing_table.xlsx

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Sr. Manager, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0124

From: Andrew Cho <andrew.cho@emergent.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: Emergent Procurement <procurement@emergent.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 12:46:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Order form: segmented entity billing, commit triggers & tax matrix

Naomi — thanks for the materials. Quick answers from our side and a couple questions: 

- PO entity: our procurement team will likely issue the PO from Emergent Solutions, Inc. but some customers chargeback to Emergent Analytics LLC for platform spend. We can supply a PO for each entity if needed.
- Tax certs: attaching our VAT registration and a corporate tax residency letter (see emergent_tax_certificates.zip).
- Net terms: procurement is pushing for Net 60 due to our approval cycles. Is Net 60 something Redwood can accommodate at scale, or would that require an executive exception?
- Billing split strawman: please provide an example invoice split (e.g., 70% to Solutions, 30% to Analytics) and how that would look operationally. Can Redwood emit two invoices for the same order form or do you prefer a single invoice with allocation detail?

Also looping in our legal lead, Maya Singh, to watch for redlines on invoicing and tax language.

Thanks,
Andrew Cho
Director, Procurement
Emergent Analytics
andrew.cho@emergent.ai

Attachment: emergent_tax_certificates.zip

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Andrew Cho <andrew.cho@emergent.ai>, Emergent Procurement <procurement@emergent.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 08:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Order form: segmented entity billing, commit triggers & tax matrix

Andrew — great, thanks for the tax docs. Short answers and a strawman attached: 

- Dual invoicing vs allocation: Redwood supports two operational approaches:
  1) Two invoices: we can issue separate invoices to two entities that sum to the committed amount (preferred if Emergent wants separate GL treatment).
  2) Single invoice with allocation lines: one invoice to a master entity with line-item allocations to different cost centers (simpler for our billing system).

- Strawman split: I attached orderform_entity_routing_table.xlsx (example shows 70/30 split by BU). If you want two invoices, we’ll need one PO per invoiced entity and matching payment instructions.

- Commit billing timing: We typically invoice the initial commit upfront, then ramp invoices at months 4 and 8 (if you want amortized billing we can indicate a monthly schedule). If Emergent prefers invoices spread over the ramp period, confirm and we’ll update the order form.

- Net terms: Net 60 is non-standard for self-serve customers but feasible for large enterprise deals with an approval path. Ben — can you confirm whether we can offer Net 60 under Commercial terms or if that requires Sales leadership sign-off?

- Taxes/withholding: we will accept Emergent’s tax certs to avoid withholding where applicable, but for countries where withholding is statutory we need an executed tax certificate and evidence of residency. For Brazil specifically, customer is responsible for withholding unless we agree to gross-up in the order form (we typically ask customers to bear withholding).

Next: Ben, if you’re OK, will prepare a short commercial redline focused on: invoice entity routing clause, net terms table, and a tax gross-up / withholding allocation sentence. I’ll then share that with Emergent’s legal.

Best,
Naomi

Attachments: orderform_entity_routing_table.xlsx (updated)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Andrew Cho <andrew.cho@emergent.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 13 May 2027 09:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Order form: segmented entity billing, commit triggers & tax matrix

Andrew / Naomi / team —

Quick commercial redline summary (attached: commercial_redlines_summary.pdf). Highlights: 

- Invoice allocation: will add an "Invoice Entity Routing" paragraph that accepts either (a) separate invoices tied to separate POs per entity, or (b) a single master invoice with explicit allocation lines. If Emergent requires dual invoices, include the PO for each invoiced entity in the purchase order submission.
- Net terms: propose Net 30 in the order form as default; we can allow Net 60 as a negotiated term under deal-specific appendix with credit approval. This protects our cashflow and gives Sales a clear escalation path.
- Minimum commits: mark them as non-refundable but eligible for credit if customer terminates with 90 days' notice; propose pro rata credit schedule in the appendix.
- Tax gross-up: we do not accept automatic gross-up in markets where customer withholding applies; instead, add a tax allocation clause that requires customer to provide tax residency docs to apply treaty relief and states customer bears withholding unless a specific gross-up is agreed in writing.
- Invoice disputes: disputes must be raised within 30 days of invoice date; undisputed portions remain payable.

If Emergent can accept the allocation approach and provide PO mapping + any continued push for Net 60 in writing, we’ll turn these into tracked redlines in the order form PDF and send for signature.

Ben Carter
Head of Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com
+1 650-555-0199

Attachment: commercial_redlines_summary.pdf

From: Andrew Cho <andrew.cho@emergent.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Emergent Procurement <procurement@emergent.ai>, Maya Singh <maya.singh@emergent.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 13 May 2027 11:04:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Order form: segmented entity billing, commit triggers & tax matrix

Thanks — appreciate the quick turnaround. Maya (cc) will review the redline summary; initial read: Emergent can accept the allocation approach (single master invoice with allocation lines) for simplicity, but procurement will push for Net 60; we can try to keep Net 30 as the baseline and move Net 60 to an approval exception documented in the deal appendix (sounds like Ben’s suggestion).

Action items:
- Emergent: confirm PO mapping by EOD Monday (we’ll see if both entities provide POs).
- Redwood: please produce a tracked-redline of the order form that folds in Ben’s bullets + the invoice allocation paragraph and an explicit line on invoice dispute timing.
- Both: schedule a 30-min call early next week to finalize net terms and the invoice flow (suggest Mon 17 May 10am PT).

Thanks,
Andrew
